name: Hub kernel
purpose: Decides how a decentralized model hub answers one file request, and whether bytes a source sent may be delivered. Send the 104-byte facts of a resolve request or the 81-byte expected and observed digest and size; it answers three bytes: the answer code, the source slot (4 for none) and the ETag kind.

promise.headline: Never hands a tool bytes that do not match, and never tells a missing repository from a private one.
promise.detail: Every answer the hub gives a file request comes from this kernel, and Lean proves its ten rules for every possible request.

claim: HK-01 to HK-10: the hub kernel's ten rules, each a theorem Lean proves for every input.

proposition.name: Accepts
proposition.text:
Accepts check :=
  SameDigest check.expected check.observed
  /\ check.expectedSize = check.observedSize
proposition.plain: Received bytes are delivered exactly when their digest and their size are the ones expected.

theorems.name: privacyHolds
theorems.statement: HK-01: a missing and a private repository get the same answer, and nothing is delivered
theorems.how: Proved by Lean with linear_arithmetic (simplify for acceptsDecides), checked by the Lean kernel and leanchecker in prismpm verify

theorems.name: deliveryHolds
theorems.statement: HK-02: a file is delivered only for a public repository at a resolved revision whose entry exists
theorems.how: Proved by Lean with linear_arithmetic (simplify for acceptsDecides), checked by the Lean kernel and leanchecker in prismpm verify

theorems.name: runnerHolds
theorems.statement: HK-03: the edge runner only redirects and the local runner only serves
theorems.how: Proved by Lean with linear_arithmetic (simplify for acceptsDecides), checked by the Lean kernel and leanchecker in prismpm verify

theorems.name: vettedHolds
theorems.statement: HK-04: the edge runner never redirects to a source that is not vetted
theorems.how: Proved by Lean with linear_arithmetic (simplify for acceptsDecides), checked by the Lean kernel and leanchecker in prismpm verify

theorems.name: sourcedHolds
theorems.statement: HK-05: a delivered file always has a source
theorems.how: Proved by Lean with linear_arithmetic (simplify for acceptsDecides), checked by the Lean kernel and leanchecker in prismpm verify

theorems.name: soundHolds
theorems.statement: HK-05: the chosen source holds the file and has not failed verification for it
theorems.how: Proved by Lean with linear_arithmetic (simplify for acceptsDecides), checked by the Lean kernel and leanchecker in prismpm verify

theorems.name: pinHolds
theorems.statement: HK-06: a pinned source is the only source the kernel may choose
theorems.how: Proved by Lean with linear_arithmetic (simplify for acceptsDecides), checked by the Lean kernel and leanchecker in prismpm verify

theorems.name: healthyHolds
theorems.statement: HK-07: without a pin, a healthy source is chosen whenever a usable one exists
theorems.how: Proved by Lean with linear_arithmetic (simplify for acceptsDecides), checked by the Lean kernel and leanchecker in prismpm verify

theorems.name: etagHolds
theorems.statement: HK-08: small files carry the git blob ETag, large files the SHA-256 ETag
theorems.how: Proved by Lean with linear_arithmetic (simplify for acceptsDecides), checked by the Lean kernel and leanchecker in prismpm verify

theorems.name: revisionHolds
theorems.statement: HK-09: a commit prefix resolves only at 7 to 40 characters and only if it matches
theorems.how: Proved by Lean with linear_arithmetic (simplify for acceptsDecides), checked by the Lean kernel and leanchecker in prismpm verify

theorems.name: acceptsDecides
theorems.statement: HK-10: accepts check = true exactly when Accepts check, for every check
theorems.how: Proved by Lean with linear_arithmetic (simplify for acceptsDecides), checked by the Lean kernel and leanchecker in prismpm verify

pinned.name: kernel_hk_01 to kernel_hk_10
pinned.what: Each theorem's exact condition, statement and axioms, that it is a build entrypoint, and that dispatch answers through the functions the theorems are about. A string-matching test, not a theorem: a planted defect fails it.
